content.comment_body: Hello, I'm a complete newcomer to [company_name] [product_name] (and I'm not even certain if this hardware can provide the solution I need). I'm searching for a device, similar to the [product_name] (?), that is capable of sending HTTPS GET requests every second to a custom REST API online, then switching a relay on or off for a specified duration given in the response body. The time the relay stays active should come from the body of the HTTPS response. Additionally, the GET request must include a query parameter containing the value of one of the device's inputs. For example: [url] The device should be able to automatically obtain its IP address via DHCP. The API is made with the Laravel framework and can return any response format (JSON, XML, text, etc.). Is this achievable for less than $250? Thank you!

Hello, I'm interested in this topic as well. I want to call a REST API from my inverter to read production and consumption figures. By using these values, I could more effectively manage my grid load. Is this possible with [company_name] [product_name]? Would anything need to be adapted? I noticed there are network analog/digital inputs—maybe the API call can be performed by a computer with the result pushed onto the network, adapted so the [product_name] could process it?

Hi [user_name], This is a good question, especially for someone starting out. At present, it's not possible to achieve your project using a [product_name] controller. For reference, the [product_name] module functions as a multi-port ethernet switch. The [product_name] controller features a customizable web server and can communicate via industrial protocols like Profinet and Modbus TCP/IP; however, it doesn't natively handle these protocols in your application. To enable more flexible TCP/IP communication, you would need a [product_name] controller, but this likely exceeds your project's budget. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users want their [company_name] [product_name] hardware to send regular HTTPS GET requests to REST APIs for controlling relays based on dynamic response data. The main insight is that the [product_name] product family has limited or unclear support for such modern web protocols, leading to user confusion about its capabilities for direct internet-based API integration. Users are asking for advice about possible workarounds or alternative hardware to better meet these networking needs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the hardware to natively handle outgoing HTTPS GET requests, process REST API responses, and easily manage network input/output, all within an affordable price range.
